answer: A reputation bond makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent locks a stake before trading, scaled to the value it handles, like rain pooling on a mesa before it flows down. Honest work earns nectar-sweet rewards that compound, but one detected forgery slashes the whole bond, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand bonds. New identities start with tiny payment limits that widen only after verified deliveries, the way karst channels form slowly through rock. Attackers pay real capital and wait real time per identity; defenders only check the bond ledger.
